entities.heading: Included entities
entities.description: Select the entities that you want to control using the scheduler. You can click on a group to open it. Note that some entities (such as sensors) can only be used for conditions, not for actions.

anchor.fixed: the same hour every day (not tied to Shabbat)

boundary.clock: at a clock time that day

detach.name: Exception
detach.note: {device} keeps its own hours here. The group leaves it alone until this ends, then takes it back.
detach.hint: Click a device to give it its own hours here.
detach.once_hint: Leave empty to repeat every week.

error.no_anchor: The plan needs its times from an entity.
error.no_anchor_hint: Enable the Jewish Calendar integration so that {start} and {end} publish a time. Halachic times are not a fixed offset from sunset, so they have to be read at trigger time rather than guessed.

help.band: The bar is one Shabbat, from candle lighting to havdalah. It is not a clock: it starts on Friday evening and ends the next night, so the same bar covers a festival that runs for two or three days.
help.rows: Each row is a group of devices that move together. Cutting a stretch in one row changes only that row — nobody else's times move.
help.detach: A device that needs different hours for a while is detached: it gets a row of its own, and while that row is running the group leaves it alone. When it ends the group takes it back, with no further action from you.
help.keys: Click a stretch to edit it. Drag the line between two stretches to move the boundary. + splits a stretch in two; Delete removes the selected one.

wizard.offer: New here? A few questions will build a working plan, and you can keep editing it afterwards.

intro.title: Let's set up your Shabbat
intro.body: You'll answer a few questions and get a working plan. Nothing is saved until you press Save at the end, and everything can be changed afterwards in the editor.

devices.title: Which devices?
devices.body: Pick the lights and switches that should follow this plan. You can add more later, and any one of them can be given its own hours afterwards.

moments.title: Build your Shabbat
moments.body: Add the moments your day is made of — dinner, bedtime, morning, lunch, a nap. Each one runs until the next. Start from a suggestion or add your own; what the devices do is the next step.
moments.name: Name it
moments.empty: No moments yet - the devices will simply hold their opening state until Shabbat goes out.

review.title: This is your Shabbat
review.body: Read it through. Anything here can still be changed in the editor afterwards.
review.outside: {names} falls outside the band and was left out. Shabbat evening times must be after candle lighting, and Shabbat day times before havdalah.

settings.title: What each device does
settings.body: Moment by moment. Set the moment as a whole with the on/off above it, then change any device that should differ — the salon air conditioner during the meal while the bedrooms stay off, one light bright and another dim.

override.label: Devices in this stretch
override.hint: Each device can do its own thing here, with its own settings — the salon air conditioner on at 16° while the bedrooms are off. A device with nothing set of its own simply follows the stretch.

enforce.label: Hold this state
enforce.hint: If a wall switch or another integration changes a device during this stretch, put it back. Waits 30 seconds between attempts so it cannot end up fighting whatever moved it.

report.title: What will happen
report.saved: Saved. This is what it will do.

book.title: Device book
book.hint: Your own names and groupings — kept in Home Assistant, so they work outside the scheduler too.

device.all_hint: A shortcut: sets every device of this group in this stretch. Each can still be changed on its own below.
device.untouched_hint: This stretch does not act on it: it keeps whatever it had, is not held to anything, is not retried, and any other schedule may drive it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.colours_hint: Plain makes on and off unmistakable at a glance. Following the action tints a stretch with the colour the bulb will actually show.
